title.orig: There is no frigate like a book
title.en: There is no frigate like a book
title.zh: 没有一艘帆船能像一本书

year_display.en: first printed 1894 (in a letter); this text 1896
year_display.zh: 1894 年首次印行（见于书信）；此为 1896 年诗集文本

edition.en: Poems, Third Series (1896), edited by Mabel Loomis Todd, on Project Gutenberg (eBook 12242)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 12242 所录《诗集·第三辑》（1896），托德编

basis.en: First printed in 1894 in Letters of Emily Dickinson, then as a poem in Poems, Third Series (1896); the author died in 1886 and the editor, Mabel Loomis Todd, in 1932.
basis.zh: 1894 年首次印行于《艾米莉·狄金森书信集》，1896 年作为诗收入《诗集·第三辑》；作者卒于 1886 年，编者梅布尔·卢米斯·托德卒于 1932 年。

note.en: Titled “A Book” by its editor. Dickinson counts the costs of travel and finds that reading is the cheapest carriage there is: no toll, open to the poorest. It is the obvious poem for a free library, and still a good one.
note.zh: 编者题为“一本书”。狄金森算了算出行的花费，发现阅读是最便宜的车马：不收过路费，最穷的人也能坐。对一座免费的图书馆来说，这是显而易见的一首，而它依然是好诗。

excerpt.orig:
There is no frigate like a book
To take us lands away,
excerpt.en:
There is no frigate like a book
To take us lands away,
excerpt.zh:
没有一艘帆船能像一本书
把我们带往远方的土地，

note.en: A neat case for reading as the cheapest travel, with lively metaphors and a fine social point; charming and apt, but well inside Dickinson’s easy range.
note.zh: 把读书说成最便宜的远行，还点出穷人也能乘坐；可爱贴切，但在狄金森轻松的音域之内。
